title: Boiler Plate [Basics]
description:
You may have noticed the large amount of stuff around the actuall text element in the last lesson. This is called _boiler plate_. This is just stuff all files have that just is required. Let's look at the boiler plate.
The default boilerplate is
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
<body>
</body>
</html>
```
Let's break this down line by line:
- `<!DOCTYPE html>`: This just defines the document type, as XML files also use a similar structure.
- `<html lang="en">`: This opens the `html` tag, which is where all your html goes. The `lang="en"` section says that it is in english.
- `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">`: The link tag takes a resource the webpage uses, in this case, a CSS file. Don't worry too much about CSS right now, but feel free to look if you want. CSS just stylizes stuff on the browser. The `rel="stylesheet"` tells the tag that this is a css file, and `href="style.css"` is where the file is located.
- `<head>`: This opens the head section of the document: This is things that can't be viewed on the page, and instead have special meanings.
- `<meta charset="UTF-8">`: This just means the HTML document is written in UTF-8 chars.
- `</head>`: This closes the head tag.
- `<body>`: This opens the `body` tag: This is where your visible HTML goes.
- `</body>`: This closes the `body` tag.
- `</html>`: This closes the `html` tag, and the document.
